milp_trigger: High demand variability (CV=0.76 > 0.75) - consider MILP for multi-echelon optimization
narrative: Material PL1__MD0FBB3A exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.756) with a statistically significant upward trend and moderate lead-time instability driven primarily by transport variability (60% of lead-time variance). The current SAP policy is severely under-stocked relative to the 95% service-level target (SS=573 vs required 2,112) and over-orders in frequency by using MOQ (91) rather than EOQ (2,244). Adopting the recommended (r,Q) policy reduces total annual cost by ~$133,786 (-84.6%) while achieving the 95% service target. Transport reliability improvement is the highest-leverage operational action to further reduce safety stock requirements.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic but largely continuous demand with moderate lead-time variability is best served by a fixed-quantity reorder-point system; EOQ balances ordering and holding costs efficiently given the high unit cost and moderate ordering cost.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Moderate - CV of 0.756 is near the lumpy threshold (1.0); if demand intermittency increases, a periodic (s,S) review or MILP-based policy should be considered.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None - storage capacity constraint is not binding (SS + OQ = 4,356 vs capacity 17,740).
